newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African bonds go to T+3 settlement from Nov 17.
newsitem.headline: S.African bonds go to T+3 settlement from Nov 17.

text.p: The Bond Exchange of South Africa said on Wednesday it would be introducing T+3 settlement from November 17, meaning bond trades will be settled on a continuous rolling basis three days after trade date.

Bond trades concluded on or before November 12 will be settled under the existing second Thursday rule. Trades on November 13 and 14 will be settled under special dispensation on November 20 while trades concluded on or after November 17 will be settled on the basis of T+3.
The exchange added that bond options written for future expiry dates must allow for exercise in accordance with the settlement practise prevailing in the underlying market at time of exercise.

Bond traders say the present lengthy settlement period encourages heavy speculative involvement in the spot market. The move to T+3 rolling settlement should stimulate increased use of both futures and the repo market, but could hit spot volumes, they added.

Rolling settlement is part of a wide-ranging programme of reform government intends to push through for the bond market. The other key element will be a new system of auctioning its stock to private market makers which it hopes to introduce during the current fiscal year.
Several foreign banks are interested in taking on the role of market-maker for government bonds.
